correction.text: The Cliopatria shape, unchanged, but holding through 318 (the year of Ptolemy's occupation) rather than ending in 319: Syria with Phoenicia, Coele-Syria and Judea, the satrapy of Laomedon

keyframe_review.note: 122 k km2 on Syria, Lebanon, Israel and Jordan (Phoenicia, Samaria, Judea, Coele-Syria): the land the Laomedon article gives him ('the important government of Syria'; Phoenicia and Coele-Syria 'attracted the interest of his powerful neighbour Ptolemy'). The shape stands; the end moves one year to 318 on the Ptolemy I page ('His first occupation of Syria was in 318'). Neither page gives an area to compare.

region.text: Syria, with Phoenicia, Coele-Syria and Judea

ledger.note: 323: Laomedon of Mytilene is given the government of Syria in the division of the provinces after Alexander's death; 'This he was still allowed to retain on the second partition at Triparadisus in 321 BC.' The page names Syria; Phoenicia, Coele-Syria and Judea are the shape's reading.

region.text: Syria, with Phoenicia, Coele-Syria and Judea: the government of Syria given to Laomedon in the division of the provinces

ledger.note: 323: Laomedon holds Syria under the empire. 'It was held at Babylon in June 323 BC'; 'All sources agree that these regions were given to' Laomedon of Mytilene (Syria), and the satraps were to 'obey the king and Perdiccas' (Partition of Babylon page); 'after the king's death in 323 BC, the important government of Syria' (Laomedon of Mytilene page), retained 'on the second partition at Triparadisus in 321 BC'. The Partition page leaves open whether the satraps were subordinate, so the vassal tint is the researcher's reading (confidence 2); it mirrors macedonian-empire /ledger/41 (c3), which carries the same event at June 323. The vassal is the satrapy itself, as in the other dossier.

region.text: Laomedon's government of Syria, invaded by Nicanor and occupied by Ptolemy

ledger.note: 318: Ptolemy occupies Syria. 'His first occupation of Syria was in 318' (Ptolemy I Soter page). The Laomedon article: Ptolemy offered money for the government, then sent Nicanor to invade Syria; 'Laomedon was unable to offer any effective resistance', was captured and sent to Egypt, escaped and joined Alcetas in Pisidia. That article gives no year; linking it to 318 is the dossier's reading.

region.text: Laomedon's government of Syria, occupied by Ptolemy

ledger.note: 318: the satrapy leaves the empire when Ptolemy occupies it. 'His first occupation of Syria was in 318' (Ptolemy I Soter page). macedonian-empire /ledger/50 ends the vassalage in 319 (Cliopatria's year, confidence 1); the 318 date is the page's, one year later, and eu-02 is asked to move theirs.
318: Laomedon's Syria passes to Ptolemy. Cliopatria's row ends in 319.

wars.name: Ptolemy's first occupation of Syria
wars.outcome: Ptolemy's general Nicanor invaded; Laomedon, unable to resist, was captured and sent to Egypt, then escaped to join Alcetas in Pisidia. Ptolemy evacuated Syria in 315 when Antigonus advanced.
wars.note: The year is the Ptolemy I Soter page's; the Laomedon article has the story without a year.

certainty.note: A satrapy's limits are administrative and approximate; no page opened draws them.

sources.title: Laomedon of Mytilene
sources.note: Identity, the government of Syria in 323, confirmed at Triparadisus in 321, Ptolemy's removal of him (no year given).

sources.title: Ptolemy I Soter
sources.note: Dates Ptolemy's first occupation of Syria to 318 and the later evacuation to 315.

sources.title: Partition of Babylon
sources.note: Repair pass: June 323, Syria to Laomedon 'all sources agree', satraps to 'obey the king and Perdiccas', the open question whether they were subordinate.

notes: Page budget two pages. Cliopatria's row (-323..-319) is kept as the outline of Syria; its end is moved to 318 on the Ptolemy I Soter page. Capital: neither page names a seat for Laomedon, so identity.capitals is empty rather than guessed. The Laomedon article does not date his removal; the Wars of the Diadochi page (opened for the ptolemaic-kingdom dossier) has no account of it either. Triparadisus (321, where Laomedon kept Syria) is the article's date; the Partition of Babylon page was opened in the repair pass (2026-10-19) for the vassal events. Seleucid and Antigonid dossiers should note that Antigonus's invasion of Syria and Phoenicia in 314-312 followed Ptolemy's occupation. After his escape Laomedon may have joined the rebels against Antigonus (the article says 'probable'); not territorial. Repair pass (2026-10-19): added vassal_start (June 323, Partition of Babylon page) and vassal_end (318, Ptolemy I Soter page) with counterpart macedonian-empire, mirroring macedonian-empire /ledger/41 and /ledger/50; the empire's vassal_end is 319 against this dossier's 318 (one year; eu-02 asked to move it). The Laomedon article does not call him a satrap or independent; the vassal status is the macedonian-empire dossier's model, followed here at confidence 2.
